_about: One Arabic root as ONE classical dictionary treats it. This is the authoring shape of a sarf_family block's data_json in ar_ling_lexicon_block — what a human fills from the book — not the header the reader sees. The header is built from this by scripts/al/build_lexicon_entry_ds.mjs in kmaps-database and travels as derived blocks; nothing below describes presentation.
_v2_note: v1 described a shape the pipeline never read (headword_line, mujarrad[] keyed by bāb, mazeed[] keyed by wazn, frames[], the bāb grid). The live spine is forms[], keyed by roman numeral. v2 documents what is actually authored and actually read.
_fill_rule: Write what the book says. Omit a key the book does not attest rather than inventing a value — the builder fills what is mechanical (see _derived) and marks it. If YOU supply something the book leaves out, keep the key and set its *_source to inferred_supplied, so the difference survives.
_scope: book — this entry speaks for this dictionary alone, never for the root at large.
_root_type: GT id. Names the root's shape (صحيح سالم، مضاعف، أجوف…), which decides which abwāb are even possible.

block_meta._core: The book's thesis for this root, in its own terms. Trilingual; ar is the book, en/ur are the gloss.
block_meta._distinctive_note: What THIS book does that its neighbours do not — where it opens, what it withholds. Renders under the book's name at the foot of the header.
block_meta._authors_own_words: The author's own opening sentence, when it is worth setting apart.

_poles: The axes this book's senses run between, in ITS order. One pole is a finding too — it says the author keeps the sense undivided — and renders as a pole, not an arrow.

forms._note: One entry per thing the book says under a form. Two entries may share a roman numeral — a general verb and a passive-only usage — and the builder merges them onto one card, so do not force them into one object here.
forms._roman: I | II | … | X. The spine. Form I is المجرَّد; II–X are المزيد فيه, and the header splits on exactly this.
forms._bab: Form I only — the six abwāb exist for it alone. The bāb IS the vowel pair (فَعَلَ يَفْعُلُ), so if the book gives madi+mudari the builder reads the bāb off them; give it here only when the book NAMES it.
forms._bab_source: attested = the book names this bāb. inferred_supplied = you supplied it; the book does not. The header marks a supplied bāb rather than passing it off as the book's.
forms._verb: Vocalize as the book does. For II–X all three are mechanical for a sound root, so omit what the book does not give and the builder fills it; for Form I only the book can say.
forms._passive: passive_form carries a passive-only usage (كُتِبَ). It needs no ماضٍ of its own — the builder nests it under its form as a sense.
forms._trans: An ATTRIBUTE of the form, never the grouping.
forms._trans_note: Where to say what the book withholds — 'al-Khalīl does not state the mudāriʿ, the bāb, or the ism al-fāʿil here'.
forms._gloss: This form's own reading, one line. Becomes the card's core line.
forms._senses: Nest under their form; the header hangs them off the card.
forms._shahid: The witness the book cites for THIS form — verse, āya, or prose. One per form; put several lines in one string as the book runs them.

_derivations: For a book that names no forms at all — Ibn Fāris runs on derivations off one aṣl. Renders as the مجرَّد section's whole content.
_nominals: The nouns the book gathers under the root. Renders as chips at the foot.
_levelling_groups: Where the book levels two forms as one sense, and who disputes it.
_defect_note: A fault in the EDITION, not in us. Shown as it stands, never silently repaired.
_provenance_keys: register and note are the pipeline talking about itself. They stay in doc_json and are never drawn.

_derived._note: NOT authored. build_lexicon_entry_ds.mjs fills these and flags each, so a reader can tell the book's word from a mechanical one. Never hand-write them into a block.
_derived.lead_ar: What names the form at the head of its line: the bāb for Form I, the form's own pattern (إِفْعَال، اِفْتِعَال) otherwise.
_derived.madi_inferred: Forms II–X: the ماضٍ is fixed per form for a sound root.
_derived.mudari_inferred: II–X from the form; Form I from its own bāb.
_derived.masadir_inferred: II–X: one canonical مصدر per form, two for III (فِعَال and مُفَاعَلة).
_derived.ism_fail_inferred: فاعل for Form I, مُفَعِّل/مُفَاعِل/… for II–X.
_derived.bab_inferred: Form I: read off the book's own ماضٍ/مضارع vowel pair.
_derived._guard: All of it is withheld for a weak, hamzated or geminate root, where the templates do not hold.
